exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: It will probably rain tomorrow.
exercises.german: Morgen wird es wahrscheinlich regnen.
exercises.why: wahrscheinlich in the open slot after the subject turns a neutral forecast into a hedge.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: The train is certain to be late today.
exercises.german: Der Zug wird heute bestimmt zu spät kommen.
exercises.why: bestimmt fixes Futur I at the strong end of the certainty scale.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: Where will she be tomorrow?
exercises.german: Wo wird sie morgen sein?
exercises.why: The wh-word takes the second position, so the finite wird follows it directly.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: Will you still be living here in five years?
exercises.german: Wirst du in fünf Jahren noch hier wohnen?
exercises.why: The particle noch fixes the future as a continuation of the present state.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: It is certain that prices will rise.
exercises.german: Es ist sicher, dass die Preise weiter steigen werden.
exercises.why: A dass-clause is verb-final, so werden steigen closes the subordinate clause.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: That will not take long.
exercises.german: Das wird nicht lange dauern.
exercises.why: Futur I in the present reference frame: nothing is finished yet, so there is no haben.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: He will probably forget about it.
exercises.german: Er wird es wahrscheinlich vergessen.
exercises.why: A negated-in-meaning prediction still takes the positive form with wahrscheinlich.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: The result will surely be better than this one.
exercises.german: Das Ergebnis wird bestimmt besser sein.
exercises.why: A comparison with a bare adjective needs no werden of its own; only werden + sein stands there.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: Nothing will come of it.
exercises.german: Es wird nichts dabei herauskommen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix detaches from the infinitive and joins the final group.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: It will not matter in the long run.
exercises.german: Auf die Dauer wird es nicht wichtig sein.
exercises.why: An impersonal mattering uses the predicate important sein after the finite wird.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: I will probably see you at the conference.
exercises.german: Ich werde dich wahrscheinlich auf der Konferenz sehen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix in the final infinitive group: an/auf ordering is set by the prefix.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: The committee will decide next week.
exercises.german: Der Ausschuss wird nächste Woche entscheiden.
exercises.why: An organisational subject in third person singular takes wird, not werden.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: That cannot be true, she will have made a mistake.
exercises.german: Das kann nicht sein, sie wird einen Fehler gemacht haben.
exercises.why: Futur II with haben draws a firm conclusion from evidence in the present frame.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: Probably nobody will come to the second session.
exercises.german: Wahrscheinlich wird niemand zur zweiten Sitzung kommen.
exercises.why: The particle may open the clause; the negated subject niemand follows the finite verb.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: When the results come in, the situation will have changed.
exercises.german: Wenn die Ergebnisse vorliegen, wird sich die Lage geändert haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense wenn-clause sets a future reference point for Futur II.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: The letter will already be on your desk tomorrow morning.
exercises.german: Der Brief wird morgen früh schon auf deinem Schreibtisch liegen.
exercises.why: schon marks the event as completed relative to a future point.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: There will probably be a lot of people there.
exercises.german: Es werden wahrscheinlich viele Leute dort sein.
exercises.why: After the expletive es the verb agrees with the subject of the clause, so the plural werden is required.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: How long will the meeting still take?
exercises.german: Wie lange wird die Besprechung noch dauern?
exercises.why: A how-long question takes the finite slot; noch asks about the remaining duration.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: The weather will probably stay bad until the weekend.
exercises.german: Das Wetter wird wahrscheinlich bis zum Wochenende schlecht bleiben.
exercises.why: A bis-phrase fixes the end of the future span; bleiben carries the state.

exercises.skill: Futur I for prediction and assumption
exercises.english: She will surely not forget the appointment.
exercises.german: Sie wird den Termin bestimmt nicht vergessen.
exercises.why: Negation after the particle weakens rather than cancels the assertion.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will call you tomorrow morning.
exercises.german: Ich werde dich morgen früh anrufen.
exercises.why: First-person werden with a separable prefix is a commitment, not a forecast.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: We will arrive in good time.
exercises.german: Wir werden rechtzeitig ankommen.
exercises.why: The inclusive wir turns the statement into a promise to the hearer.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I promise to be there by eight.
exercises.german: Ich verspreche, dass ich pünktlich bin.
exercises.why: versprechen governs a dass-clause, and its verb stands last without a future form.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: Do not worry, I will handle it.
exercises.german: Keine Sorge, ich kümmere mich darum.
exercises.why: A literal promise drops Futur I in favour of the present tense.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: He will pay for the damage.
exercises.german: Er wird für den Schaden aufkommen.
exercises.why: Third-person werden in a commitment context still reads as a firm announcement.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: We are going to need more time.
exercises.german: Wir werden mehr Zeit brauchen.
exercises.why: A von-subclass verb such as brauchen keeps its infinitive at the end of the clause.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will send you the documents this evening.
exercises.german: Ich werde dir heute Abend die Unterlagen schicken.
exercises.why: The dative pronoun precedes the accusative noun phrase in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: Nothing will change, I give you my word.
exercises.german: Unsere Pläne werden sich nicht ändern.
exercises.why: A negated sich ändern fixes the outcome, so the Future form reads as a commitment rather than a forecast.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: She will not forget your birthday, I am certain.
exercises.german: Sie wird deinen Geburtstag bestimmt nicht vergessen.
exercises.why: A reassurance in the third person still leans on the particle to signal the speaker's commitment.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: We will keep you informed.
exercises.german: Wir werden dich auf dem Laufenden halten.
exercises.why: An idiom in the final group; the separable prefix of the infinitive stays attached.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will take care of the tickets.
exercises.german: Ich werde die Tickets besorgen.
exercises.why: A simple decision reported as a promise needs no hedging particle.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: They will move into the new flat in autumn.
exercises.german: Sie werden im Herbst in die neue Wohnung ziehen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix plus a directional complement stays together in the final group.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will do my best.
exercises.german: Ich werde mein Bestes tun.
exercises.why: The idiom takes a bare accusative object in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: We will never forget that evening.
exercises.german: Wir werden diesen Abend nie vergessen.
exercises.why: The temporal object is an accusative demonstrative; nie negates the future, not the past.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: He will bring the drinks.
exercises.german: Er wird die Getränke mitbringen.
exercises.why: A separable prefix joined to the final noun by nothing: mitbringen is one unit here.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: You will hear from me next week.
exercises.german: Du wirst nächste Woche von mir hören.
exercises.why: The idiom hören von takes dative: von mir, not von mich.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will not go without you.
exercises.german: Ich werde nicht ohne dich gehen.
exercises.why: Negation of the infinitive, with the prepositional phrase in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: Everything will be fine, really.
exercises.german: Es wird schon alles in Ordnung sein.
exercises.why: schon reassures and softens, so the promise need not be hedged further.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: We will celebrate properly next year.
exercises.german: Wir werden nächstes Jahr ordentlich feiern.
exercises.why: A separable-free infinitive after an adverb in the middle field.

exercises.skill: Futur I for promise and intention
exercises.english: I will speak to him about it.
exercises.german: Ich werde mit ihm darüber sprechen.
exercises.why: Two prepositional phrases bracket the subject, leaving the verb group intact.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the time you arrive, I will have finished the report.
exercises.german: Bis du ankommst, werde ich den Bericht fertig haben.
exercises.why: A bis-clause in the present marks the future reference point for Futur II.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the end of the year, the company will have doubled its staff.
exercises.german: Bis Ende des Jahres wird das Unternehmen seinen Personalbestand verdoppelt haben.
exercises.why: An accusative object and a participle join the final group after werden.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: In ten years, the climate will have changed dramatically.
exercises.german: In zehn Jahren wird sich das Klima dramatisch verändert haben.
exercises.why: A future time adverb is enough on its own to require the retrospective future.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By then, she will have written her dissertation.
exercises.german: Bis dahin wird sie ihre Dissertation geschrieben haben.
exercises.why: ge- reappears before the participle, which is separated from its prefix by werden.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: In 2050, nobody will know anything about this scandal.
exercises.german: Im Jahr 2050 wird niemand mehr etwas von diesem Skandal wissen.
exercises.why: A negated subject with a negated verb still needs the Futur II form.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the time you get here, the weather will have changed completely.
exercises.german: Bis du hier eintrifft, wird sich das Wetter völlig verändert haben.
exercises.why: A reflexive verb in Futur II with haben, not with sein.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By 2030, most people will have stopped using cash.
exercises.german: Bis 2030 werden die meisten Menschen aufgehört haben, Bargeld zu benutzen.
exercises.why: The zu-infinitive may follow the bare participle in the final group.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: In a week, the editorial team will have published the figures.
exercises.german: Die Redaktion wird die Zahlen in einer Woche bereits veröffentlicht haben.
exercises.why: A perfect participle in the final group; bereits stresses that the action is already finished.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the time the guests arrive, the hostess will have set the table.
exercises.german: Bis die Gäste eintreffen, wird die Gastgeberin den Tisch gedeckt haben.
exercises.why: A bis-clause in the present plus an active Futur II in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the time we meet again, the situation will have changed completely.
exercises.german: Wenn wir uns wiedersehen, wird sich die Lage völlig geändert haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense wenn-clause and a reflexive Futur II with haben in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: Once the application arrives, we will have processed it.
exercises.german: Sobald der Antrag eingeht, werden wir ihn bearbeitet haben.
exercises.why: A separable prefix in the subclause and a prefixed participle in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: At the end of next month, she will have finished her training.
exercises.german: Ende nächsten Monats wird sie ihre Ausbildung abgeschlossen haben.
exercises.why: An adverbial of time opens the clause, the subject follows, and the verb group closes it.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By Sunday, the new rules will already have been applied.
exercises.german: Bis Sonntag wird man das neue Regelwerk bereits angewendet haben.
exercises.why: man plus Futur II renders a passive without needing a passive form.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By then, people will have forgotten these buildings.
exercises.german: Bis dahin wird man diese Gebäude vergessen haben.
exercises.why: man plus Futur II reports the finished state of a past event from a future vantage point.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: Once the reconstruction is finished, much will have changed.
exercises.german: Bis der Wiederaufbau abgeschlossen sein wird, wird sich viel verändert haben.
exercises.why: A bis-clause in Futur I sets the same future reference point from the other side.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By 2028, the population will have halved.
exercises.german: Bis 2028 wird sich die Bevölkerung halbiert haben.
exercises.why: A reflexive verb with haben; halbieren is not a change-of-state verb here.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By the anniversary, the whole story will have been forgotten.
exercises.german: Bis zum Jubiläum wird man die Geschichte vergessen haben.
exercises.why: A bis-phrase with an article phrase in the accusative after zum.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: When she returns from abroad, she will have completed her degree.
exercises.german: Wenn sie aus dem Ausland zurückkommt, wird sie ihr Studium abgeschlossen haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense wenn-clause; the participle takes the ge- of its verb stem.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: By December, the company will have completed its move.
exercises.german: Bis Dezember wird das Unternehmen seinen Umzug abgeschlossen haben.
exercises.why: A separable prefix in the participle, placed inside the final verb group.

exercises.skill: Futur II for a completed future-past event
exercises.english: After ten years of research, the team will have found a cure.
exercises.german: Nach zehn Jahren Forschung wird das Team ein Heilmittel gefunden haben.
exercises.why: A temporal preposition in front, an accusative object in the middle field, verb group last.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If I had known that, I would have told you.
exercises.german: Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, hätte ich es dir gesagt.
exercises.why: The unreal condition takes the preterite of haben and the main clause the Konjunktiv II.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If she had asked, I would have helped her.
exercises.german: Wenn sie gefragt hätte, hätte ich ihr geholfen.
exercises.why: The verb of the wenn-clause stands last, and hätte is the preterite, not a perfect form.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
exercises.german: Wenn wir früher gegangen wären, hätten wir den Zug bekommen.
exercises.why: A counterfactual movement verb in the preterite with the Konjunctive II auxiliary wären.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If he had studied more, he would have found a job.
exercises.german: Wenn er mehr gelernt hätte, hätte er eine Stelle gefunden.
exercises.why: Two finite forms of the same verb in different positions keep the two clauses apart.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If you had warned me, I would not have gone there.
exercises.german: Wenn du mich gewarnt hättest, wäre ich nicht dorthin gegangen.
exercises.why: A negated Konjunktiv II main clause with the infinitive of gehen standing last.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If they had arrived earlier, they would have seen the exhibition.
exercises.german: Wenn sie früher gekommen wären, hätten sie die Ausstellung noch gesehen.
exercises.why: A past participle in the Konjunktiv II main clause; the subordinate verb is preterite.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If we had not booked in time, the hotel would have been full.
exercises.german: Wenn wir nicht rechtzeitig gebucht hätten, wäre das Hotel ausgebucht gewesen.
exercises.why: A negated preterite clause in front, so the finite verb follows it immediately.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If I had taken the 6:15 train, I would have been on time.
exercises.german: Wenn ich den Zug um 6.15 Uhr genommen hätte, wäre ich pünktlich gewesen.
exercises.why: A time expression inside the subordinate clause does not disturb its final verb.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If the weather had been better, we would have gone hiking.
exercises.german: Wenn das Wetter besser gewesen wäre, wären wir wandern gegangen.
exercises.why: sein in the preterite of a state; the main clause keeps Konjunktiv II rather than Futur II.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If he had slept longer, he would not have missed the flight.
exercises.german: Wenn er länger geschlafen hätte, hätte er den Flug nicht verpasst.
exercises.why: Two separable-free infinitives, one in each clause, both at the very end.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If we had asked her, she would have helped us.
exercises.german: Wenn wir sie gefragt hätten, hätte sie uns geholfen.
exercises.why: The object pronoun precedes the subject pronoun in the main clause as usual.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: When the concert begins, we will already have been waiting for an hour.
exercises.german: Wenn das Konzert beginnt, werden wir schon eine Stunde gewartet haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense wenn-clause fixes the future reference point; the durative main clause needs Futur II.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If you had asked me yesterday, you will have heard the whole story.
exercises.german: Wenn du mich gestern gefragt hättest, wirst du die ganze Geschichte gehört haben.
exercises.why: The wenn-clause is unreal and so takes Konjunktiv II, while the main clause is Futur II.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If I had known the answer, I would have said so at the time.
exercises.german: Wenn ich die Antwort gewusst hätte, hätte ich es damals gesagt.
exercises.why: The adverbial sits behind the pronoun in the main clause; the verb still comes first.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: When the reconstruction is done, the museum will have reopened.
exercises.german: Wenn der Wiederaufbau beendet ist, wird das Museum wiedereröffnet haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense wenn-clause; a prefixed participle closes the Futur II main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If he had listened to me, he would still be working there.
exercises.german: Wenn er auf mich gehört hätte, würde er heute noch dort arbeiten.
exercises.why: A separable prefix in the subordinate clause, and a modal in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If we had left the port earlier, we would have missed the storm.
exercises.german: Wenn wir den Hafen früher verlassen hätten, hätten wir den Sturm verpasst.
exercises.why: A strong-verb preterite in the wenn-clause, a perfect participle in the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If the deadline had been later, I could have submitted it.
exercises.german: Wenn die Frist später gewesen wäre, hätte ich es abgeben können.
exercises.why: The modal infinitive at the end may stand after a full infinitive group.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: When the invoice is paid, the customer will have received his refund.
exercises.german: Sobald die Rechnung bezahlt ist, wird der Kunde sein Geld zurückbekommen haben.
exercises.why: A present-tense sobald-clause marks the reference point; the prefixed participle closes the main clause.

exercises.skill: Futur II with time clauses (wenn + Präteritum)
exercises.english: If I had understood the question, I would have answered differently.
exercises.german: Wenn ich die Frage verstanden hätte, hätte ich anders geantwortet.
exercises.why: Two strong-verb preterites with identical auxiliary forms, separated by their objects.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: I am going to leave now.
exercises.german: Ich gehe jetzt.
exercises.why: A neutral future with a time expression needs no future form at all.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: She is going to call you tomorrow.
exercises.german: Sie wird dich morgen anrufen.
exercises.why: Present werden plus infinitive, the plain future of a plan rather than a forecast.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The new bus line will start running on Monday.
exercises.german: Ab Montag fährt die neue Buslinie.
exercises.why: Present tense plus a time adverb: the standard written German future.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: There will be no class next Tuesday.
exercises.german: Am nächsten Dienstag findet kein Unterricht statt.
exercises.why: Present of finden as a neutral future, with negation carried by kein.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: I will have time for a coffee tomorrow.
exercises.german: Morgen habe ich Zeit für einen Kaffee.
exercises.why: Present haben plus a time expression means the same as a Futur I prediction.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: We are moving house in the summer.
exercises.german: Wir ziehen im Sommer um.
exercises.why: A separable prefix detaches before the time adverb and rejoins the final group.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: Are you going to come to the party?
exercises.german: Kommst du zu Annas Geburtstagsfeier?
exercises.why: The present tense in a question is neutral between present and future meaning.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The meeting will start at nine.
exercises.german: Die Besprechung beginnt um neun.
exercises.why: A timetable statement; a present-tense form is more idiomatic than any future form.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: I am writing to her this week.
exercises.german: Ich schreibe ihr diese Woche einen Brief.
exercises.why: A present intention with an accusative object in the middle field.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: It will probably snow tonight.
exercises.german: Heute Abend schneit es vielleicht.
exercises.why: vielleicht can accompany a present tense just as well as a Futur I form.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: What are you going to do this weekend?
exercises.german: Was machst du dieses Wochenende?
exercises.why: Present of machen in an interrogative with a temporal expression.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: Prices will go up next year.
exercises.german: Nächstes Jahr steigen die Preise.
exercises.why: A present-tense rise with a future time adverb is a neutral statement of fact.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: She is going to study medicine.
exercises.german: Sie studiert Medizin.
exercises.why: A present-tense plan with an accusative field of study.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The library will close at eight.
exercises.german: Die Bibliothek schließt um acht.
exercises.why: A closing time is given in the present, not with werden.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The children will go to school by bike.
exercises.german: Die Kinder fahren mit dem Fahrrad zur Schule.
exercises.why: Present tense plus a modal phrase of means in the middle field.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The train will depart from platform three.
exercises.german: Der Zug fährt von Gleis drei ab.
exercises.why: The separable prefix of abfahren stands last, after the platform phrase.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: You are going to regret that.
exercises.german: Das wirst du bereuen.
exercises.why: Present of werden with a predicative adjective and no infinitive at all.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The letter will arrive tomorrow morning.
exercises.german: Morgen früh liegt der Brief im Postfach.
exercises.why: Present of liegen with a place phrase: a neutral future needing no future form at all.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: The law will come into force in July.
exercises.german: Das Gesetz tritt im Juli in Kraft.
exercises.why: A fixed legal idiom, fixed time, present tense: no future form belongs here.

exercises.skill: werden + Infinitiv as a substitute for Futur
exercises.english: Prices will keep rising for a while yet.
exercises.german: Die Preise werden weiter steigen.
exercises.why: Present werden with an adverb and no infinitive: a process already under way.
